lines.text: Maric stood in the middle of the training yard, burning. Not gold, like the fire he'd lit at sixteen. White. White as the inside of a forge.
Six straw men stood around him. As I watched, they went up one after another, like candles.
Look, little brother! Look what I can do now! Five rings? This is more than five! This is what a Varr is supposed to be!
Ilse had come down behind me in her nightgown and headscarf, without her spectacles, squinting into the glare.
That isn't his fire, Lucan. It's burning him. Look at his hands.
His hands were blistering. The fire was eating him from the inside, and he was laughing.
Then the light went out of him all at once, like a snuffed candle. And my brother fell down in the sand.
I got to him first. He was shaking, and grey, and cold as the river. Empty. Just like the people in the grey village.
Maric! Maric, look at me!
I knew what I could do. I had done it for a little girl in a barn. I had done it for a whole keep at Kesting.
Maric. Listen to me. Let me claim you.
Accept me, and you'll heal. You'll grow. Real rings, your own, not out of a bottle. You don't have to say anything. You only have to mean it.
Claim me? Like your farmers? Like your dog?
I don't need your charity.
A claim needs two people. I could pour everything I had into him, and it would run off him like rain off a roof. I held his hand anyway. He pulled it away.
Father carried him inside himself. He wouldn't let the servants touch him.
Go to the King, Lucan, if you must. I'll keep him alive. I've been keeping him alive for months.
You knew. About the draught.
The Order gives, and the Order takes. Every house in Aldmere knows it. Nobody says it.
We left at dawn, on a Varr barge flying black and gold. Corvin had packed food, and three bottles of my father's best wine. He said my father owed me seventeen years of birthday presents.
As the barge pulled away, I looked back at the keep. Maric was on the wall, alone, wrapped in a blanket, watching me go.
And as I watched, he lifted the little white vial to his lips, and drank.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty-eight, coming soon.
